OPEN LEMMA of block 33 (PR #8177; setting in blocks 25, 30, 32: PRs #8168, #8174, #8176). Two-level noisy majority automaton in level time on Z^3: a site's three predecessors are z - e_1, z - e_2, z - e_3; seeds S (no 1-predecessor), amplified sites A (exactly one), processed sites (two or more). It is equivalent to the unit budget c* = 1 and would lower the proved ordering threshold on the line (p,1,2) from 4165 to 453. Evidence: no violation in about 10^4 hill-climbed realizations; structural searches found no tight sibling pairs at all. title: Repair block 17's chessboard step and find the true constant
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Repair block 17's chessboard step and find the true constant. DEFECT found by a probe and confirmed (issue list: J:attack:PR8151): in block 17 (PR #8151, the static six-axis law's ordered side) T3 disseminates the event 'the canonical direction-i bond of the cell is bad' by reflections through site planes and states the result as 'every direction-i bond is bad'. Site reflections preserve the parity of the transverse coordinates, so the realized event is the direction-i bonds with even transverse coordinates (N/2 in 2D, N/4 in 3D), and T4's epsilon = 6m/p, hence T7's threshold p >= 216 max(q,r), does not follow. TASK: a correct chain with the best constant you can prove. Candidates: (i) a lemma that recovers the 2D statement (combine the four parity classes by a second chessboard or by Cauchy-Schwarz over classes); (ii) reflections through BOND planes (planes between sites): decide exactly for which weights (p, q, r) the six-axis law is reflection positive there, since those reflections move parity; (iii) cells of side two, so that one cell carries all parity classes; (iv) a Peierls count on the coarser lattice of even sites. COMPUTED LEAD for (ii): reflection positivity through a bond plane needs the 6 x 6 weight matrix W (p same axis, q opposite, r orthogonal) positive semidefinite; its eigenvalues are p+q+4r, p-q (three times), p+q-2r (twice), so the condition is p >= q and p + q >= 2r: on the line (p,1,2) that is p >= 3, the whole regime of interest; bond reflections move the parity that site reflections preserve. LEAD (executed on small lattices on 2026-09-18, not proved). The campaign studied the formation law on Z^3 in level order: two-dimensional level planes, where the sphere menu loses its memory (block 26, PR #8170) and the equal-level kernel is a plane Green function, logarithmic (block 35, PR #8180). On the event lattice Z^4 (a record at x formed from x - e_1, ..., x - e_4; level planes three-dimensional) the linear theory changes character: the plane walk is transient, the zero-mode sum (2 pi)^-3 Int 1/(1 - |phi|^2), phi = (1 + e^{ik1} + e^{ik2} + e^{ik3})/4, is finite, and the equal-level transverse covariance sigma^2/(1 - |phi(k)|^2) ~ sigma^2/(k^T M k) is a THREE-dimensional Green function: a 1/r law at equal level, the kernel the gravity node asks for, now under the axiom's own reading. Simulation (probes/lib/formation_levelplane.py): at beta = 6 the 3+1 sphere law holds |m| = 0.93 and its structure factor matches the linear kernel within a few percent. TASK: theorems. (a) Long-range order: prove that the sphere formation law on Z^4 in level order, started from an aligned plane, keeps liminf_t E[m_t . e] > 0 for beta large (routes: a comparison of the transverse field with the linear model using block 27's sign lemma, A(kappa)/kappa decreasing; an energy-entropy or chessboard argument in level time; a Lyapunov function for the plane average). title: Does the law depend on the order in which causally unrelated records form?
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Does the law depend on the order in which causally unrelated records form?. On an event lattice the axiom fixes that a record is formed from its recorded predecessors; records at the same level are causally unrelated. TASK: prove that for ANY event lattice with a finite predecessor set and ANY formation order compatible with the causal order (not only level by level), the joint law of the records is the same, because each record's law depends only on its predecessors' values (a product of kernels along the partial order); state the exact hypothesis needed (every predecessor recorded before its successor; no record re-formed) and exhibit the smallest example where an order that violates it changes the law. title: The ordered side of the six-axis law under light-cone formation, by equilibrium methods

SETTING (the owner's working reading, 2026-09-20; block 39, the open PR titled 'ail39: records that move'): a site is empty or carries ONE record; a record carries its content (six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega, omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal axes; a bond with an empty end weighs 1; the axioms' rule K (normalized over contents) does not depend on the scale c. MOTION: a record chooses between its position and an empty neighbouring position in proportion to the pair weights it would have there; this is in detailed balance with the static law on the occupied set. The neutral scale c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r): an empty neighbour weighs what a record of random content weighs on average, and it is the least scale at which the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes. Simulator: probes/lib/moving_gas.py p q r scale rho L sweeps seed (scale = a number or the word neutral). The owner's remark: a region does not have to be very full to jam, and a jammed region is where nothing can happen any more. Under pair-weight transit a record with k agreeing neighbours leaves with probability 1/(1 + (c p)^k), and a record with no empty neighbour cannot move at all. TASK: for a convex cluster of aligned records in empty space, with rare formation at rate z Z_x: (a) which records can ever move (the surface), and how the number of arrangements reachable in a time T scales with the cluster's volume and with its surface; (b) the growth law of the cluster by sticking and by formation at its surface, and its evaporation rate, as functions of its size; is there a size above which a cluster only grows? (c) whether contents inside are frozen forever, and what an observer who can read only records (the axioms: only records are readable) can learn about the interior from the surface. State theorems for finite clusters with exact small checks; no identification with anything in nature is asked for. title: The sphere menu with vacancies at the pinned scale: long-range order and the stiffness of the kernel
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 5: The sphere menu with vacancies at the pinned scale: long-range order and the stiffness of the kernel. SETTING (blocks 39 and 40, open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move' and 'ail40'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record; two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega the rule's pair weights), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; motion is pair-weight transit, in detailed balance with this law; formation happens at rate z * Z_x with content drawn from the rule. THE PINNED SCALE: c = c_0, the value at which W is the rule's one-neighbour probability divided by the uniform probability (six axes: c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r), W = 6 K_1; sphere menu with omega = exp(beta s.s'): c_0 = beta/sinh(beta), W = the density of the rule against the uniform measure). At c_0: an empty site acts on each neighbour as a record of unknown content; the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes (and not below c_0); on any window without a cycle the occupancies are independent with density 6z/(1 + 6z); a fully occupied cycle of length n carries the factor 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n with l_1 = (p - q)/(p + q + 4r), l_2 = (p + q - 2r)/(p + q + 4r). The owner has accepted c = c_0 as the working value; it is not registered. This is the route by which a one-over-distance potential would come back under the moving-records reading. Block 19 (PR #8153) proved for the FULL-lattice sphere law: bond-plane reflection positivity, the domination of the twisted partition function, the infrared bound and long-range order above a coupling. title: The halo of a producing lump: its strength against the lump's record count
what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 5: The halo of a producing lump: its strength against the lump's record count. SETTING (blocks 39, 40, 41; open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move', 'ail40', 'ail41: what a source is'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record (content = one of the six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal contents), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; the neutral scale is c_0 = 6/(p+q+4r), at which every row of W sums to 6 and records do not bind on any window without a cycle (all binding is the loop factor 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n, l_1 = (p-q)/(p+q+4r), l_2 = (p+q-2r)/(p+q+4r)). what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 1 of 4: Inertia without re-drawing contents: is there a clause with waves in which no record's content ever changes?. SETTING (blocks 43 and 44; open PRs titled 'ail43: the fields of the record layer arrive by diffusion' and 'ail44: records with inertia'): block 43 showed that the two fields found in the record layer settle by a random walk (a distance R costs about R^2 ticks), so a carrier of a long-range field needs a speed. BLOCK 44's CLAUSE (supplied, not adopted): a record's content is its direction of travel. (S) each record at rate 1 tries to step along its content (six-axis menu: to x + e_d; sphere menu: to x + e_k with probability max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3); an empty target is entered; an occupied target exchanges contents with the record (the two pass through each other); a solid site reflects it. (C) each bond at rate gamma re-draws the contents of its two records uniformly on their momentum class (six axes: an opposite pair becomes a uniformly random opposite pair, any other pair is exchanged with probability 1/2; sphere: P/2 +- r w, w uniform on the unit circle orthogonal to P = s + s', r^2 = 1 - |P|^2/4). PROVED: number of records and momentum (sum of the contents' unit vectors) are conserved by every event; the clause is covariant; the UNIFORM measure is stationary (every record has exactly one streaming preimage; the scattering kernel is symmetric), also with reflecting bodies, and NOT if blocked attempts do nothing or if head-on pairs scatter when an attempt is blocked; in product states the mass current is (1 - rho) g and the pressure is exactly rho/3, so the linearized Euler speed squared is (1 - rho)/3 (six axes) and (1 - rho)/9 (sphere); in equilibrium the mean force on a reflecting body is exactly zero. EXECUTED: standing waves oscillate at 0.467 vs 0.483 (six axes) and 0.277 vs 0.279 (sphere) at density 0.3; bodies that CAPTURE records attract each other; bodies that emit records were also measured. The simulators are probes/lib/inertial.py (both menus: tick6, tick_s, sound) and probes/lib/inertial_bodies.py (two bodies in the sphere-menu gas: usage inertial_bodies.py L rho0 radius separation Q ticks seed gamma [absorb] [single]). TASK: block 44's scattering (C) re-draws contents in an encounter, against the plain reading of the Record axiom ('a record locks exactly one admissible local possibility'). Without (C) the clause is pass-through streaming only. (a) Prove that under (S) alone the six contents are six independent totally asymmetric exclusion streams (each species is blocked only by its own species), give the exact hydrodynamic equation of each stream (density current rho_d (1 - rho_d)) and show that a standing density wave along x does not oscillate as a sound wave: compute its exact linear evolution. (b) Classify the covariant, number- and momentum-conserving nearest-neighbour encounter rules in which contents never change (records may only move or swap sites); decide whether any of them thermalizes momentum; prove the answer. (c) If none does, state the theorem: in the six-axis menu, waves need re-drawing; and say what the weakest re-drawing is (only opposite pairs? only on a bond clock?) for which the uniform measure stays stationary. check.py: exact enumeration on the 3^3 torus with two and three records. SETTING (blocks 43 and 44; open PRs titled 'ail43: the fields of the record layer arrive by diffusion' and 'ail44: records with inertia'): block 43 showed that the two fields found in the record layer settle by a random walk (a distance R costs about R^2 ticks), so a carrier of a long-range field needs a speed. BLOCK 44's CLAUSE (supplied, not adopted): a record's content is its direction of travel. (S) each record at rate 1 tries to step along its content (six-axis menu: to x + e_d; sphere menu: to x + e_k with probability max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3); an empty target is entered; an occupied target exchanges contents with the record (the two pass through each other); a solid site reflects it. (C) each bond at rate gamma re-draws the contents of its two records uniformly on their momentum class (six axes: an opposite pair becomes a uniformly random opposite pair, any other pair is exchanged with probability 1/2; sphere: P/2 +- r w, w uniform on the unit circle orthogonal to P = s + s', r^2 = 1 - |P|^2/4). PROVED: number of records and momentum (sum of the contents' unit vectors) are conserved by every event; the clause is covariant; the UNIFORM measure is stationary (every record has exactly one streaming preimage; the scattering kernel is symmetric), also with reflecting bodies, and NOT if blocked attempts do nothing or if head-on pairs scatter when an attempt is blocked; in product states the mass current is (1 - rho) g and the pressure is exactly rho/3, so the linearized Euler speed squared is (1 - rho)/3 (six axes) and (1 - rho)/9 (sphere); in equilibrium the mean force on a reflecting body is exactly zero. EXECUTED: standing waves oscillate at 0.467 vs 0.483 (six axes) and 0.277 vs 0.279 (sphere) at density 0.3; bodies that CAPTURE records attract each other; bodies that emit records were also measured. The simulators are probes/lib/inertial.py (both menus: tick6, tick_s, sound) and probes/lib/inertial_bodies.py (two bodies in the sphere-menu gas: usage inertial_bodies.py L rho0 radius separation Q ticks seed gamma [absorb] [single]). TASK: block 44's scattering (C) re-draws contents in an encounter, against the plain reading of the Record axiom ('a record locks exactly one admissible local possibility'). Without (C) the clause is pass-through streaming only. (a) Prove that under (S) alone the six contents are six independent totally asymmetric exclusion streams (each species is blocked only by its own species), give the exact hydrodynamic equation of each stream (density current rho_d (1 - rho_d)) and show that a standing density wave along x does not oscillate as a sound wave: compute its exact linear evolution. (b) Classify the covariant, number- and momentum-conserving nearest-neighbour encounter rules in which contents never change (records may only move or swap sites); decide whether any of them thermalizes momentum; prove the answer. (c) If none does, state the theorem: in the six-axis menu, waves need re-drawing; and say what the weakest re-drawing is (only opposite pairs? only on a bond clock?) for which the uniform measure stays stationary. check.py: exact enumeration on the 3^3 torus with two and three records.
